title: Garikapati Veeraya v. N. Subbiah Choudhry

content.caseIdentity: Garikapati Veeraya v. N. Subbiah Choudhry, AIR 1957 SC 540
content.facts: A suit was instituted prior to the commencement of the Constitution of India. An appeal arose after the Constitution came into force, raising the question of whether the right of appeal was governed by the pre-existing law or the new constitutional appellate provisions.
questionsBeforeCourt: Whether the right of appeal is a vested right that arises at the date of the initiation of proceedings, and whether a new procedural enactment extinguishes that vested right.
content.ratioDecidendi: The right of appeal is not a mere matter of procedure but is a substantive right. The institution of the suit or criminal proceeding carries with it the implication that all rights of appeal then in force are preserved to the parties until the rest of the career of the suit. This vested right can be taken away only by a subsequent enactment if it so provides expressly or by necessary intendment, and not otherwise.
content.holding: Held that the right of appeal is governed by the law in force at the time of the institution of the proceeding.
content.relevance: The foundational authority establishing that appeals arising from trials pending on 30 June 2024 remain substantively governed by the 1973 CrPC under Section 531(2)(a).
